item.title: Leaked data shows 490,000 Russian forces have died in Ukraine war
item.description:
More than 490,000 Russian soldiers have died since Vladimir Putin ordered Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, according to leaked Russian government data analyzed by CBS News partner network BBC News. Another organization's analysis of the vast dataset suggests the toll is likely closer to 700,000.
A recent hack by pro-Ukraine groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine's Silent Crow produced the data that was analyzed by the BBC and independent Russian outlet Mediazona. It included more than 11 million death records from 2021 to September 2026, according to the British broadcaster.
The data, which includes granular information on the location of deaths in Ukraine and Russian border regions, age ranges, causes of death, and employment and court rulings suggests at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died during the war so far, according to the BBC. According to Mediazona's analysis, which the outlet said accounted for delays in death registrations, missing records and deaths occurring since the data was leaked, Russia's total military death toll has likely reached around 700,000.
In May, the head of the United Kingdom's communications and cyber spy agency also put the number of Russian military deaths during the war at about 500,000, citing Western intelligence.
"Putin is going backwards on the battlefield, with new intelligence showing that almost half a million Russian soldiers have been killed since the conflict began," Anne Keast-Butler, the director of the Government Communications Headquarters (GCHQ), said at the time.

item.title: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI in war
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Iran's U.N. ambassador on Tuesday criticized the U.S. military's use of artificial intelligence systems in the nearly 9-month war, claiming American forces leveraged the technology to plan and carry out some 2,000 attacks over just four days.The Iran-backed Houthi group claimed an attack on the financial district of Saudi Arabia's capital on Wednesday, as well on a sprawling oil refinery in the country's east.Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday that Iran is developing chemical weapons and vowed to stop Tehran from obtaining them. Iran has repeatedly denied it is developing chemical weapons.
New Updates
2:08 PM
Iran criticizes Sen. Cornyn for incorrectly citing nuclear report actually about North Korea
The Iranian Foreign Ministry has called out Republican Sen. John Cornyn for a post on X criticizing Iran's alleged pursuit of nuclear weapons, however, the quote cited by the senator was actually about North Korean nuclear ambitions.
The Texas senator cited International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi raising concern "about a rapidly built extension at the Yongbyon gas centrifuge uranium enrichment plant."
Cornyn wrote on X, "Doesn't sound like the Iranian regime is giving up on its nuclear weapons aspirations."
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei correctly pointed out Grossi was speaking about Yongbyon, North Korea, and nothing to do with Iran.

item.title: "Narco sub" seized in Atlantic but no drugs found on board
item.description:
The French navy intercepted a semi-submersible craft suspected of involvement in drug trafficking in the Atlantic Ocean, a prosecutor said Wednesday, days after stopping a similar "narco sub" carrying several tons of cocaine.
"The semi-submersible was flying no flag and was suspected of being involved in drug trafficking" when French forces intercepted it on November 17, said organized crime prosecutor Vanessa Perree.
No drugs were found but "the vessel's location, lack of flag, its clandestine nature and items discovered onboard" led to the arrest of two crew members, she added.
The operation was carried out in cooperation with the Colombian navy and the U.S. Joint Interagency Task Force South.
The vessel's seizure "deals a serious blow to the drug traffickers' logistics." said Perree.
Catherine Vautrin, the country's armed forces minister, hailed the operation in a social media post, which included images of the vessel.
The French navy intercepted a semi-submersible craft suspected of involvement in drug trafficking in the Atlantic Ocean, officials said.
Catherine Vautrin, France's armed forces minister
"The French armed forces are maintaining their efforts in the fight against drug trafficking networks," she wrote on X. "With this intervention by the Armed Forces in the French Antilles, an entire criminal network and its associated logistics have been disrupted."
Narco subs, which cannot go fully underwater, are popular among international drug traffickers as they can sometimes elude detection by law enforcement.

item.title: Titanic postcard sent days before doomed voyage sells for pricey sum
item.description:
A rare postcard from a Titanic crew member that features the famed ocean liner and was sent less than a week before its doomed voyage in 1912 sold at auction for over $41,000, according to a U.K. auction house.
The postcard from Jack Phillips, the Titanic's chief radio officer, was postmarked April 6, 1912, four days before the ill-fated ship set sail on its maiden voyage across the Atlantic from Southampton, England, for New York City.
Phillips, who turned 25 on the ship, sent the postcard to his sister, Elsie Phillips, according to auction house Henry Aldridge and Son Ltd.
"Thanks very much for your letter. Having glorious weather, went to Cowes yesterday. Will write later before we sail. Love all, Jack," Phillips wrote on the back of the postcard.
Jack Phillips wrote to his sister, Elsie Phillips, on a Titanic postcard that was postmarked April 6, 1912.
Henry Aldridge and Son Ltd.
The front features a picture of the Titanic at Southampton in southern England. The auction house said the postcard was in "very good to fine condition, with some light soiling and toning."
The Titanic is seen on a postcard that was postmarked April 6, 1912.
Henry Aldridge and Son Ltd.
According to the auction house, the postcard sold for 32,000 British pounds, or around $41,800. With taxes and fees, the final cost was 40,000 pounds, or around $52,300.
During the trans-Atlantic crossing, on the night of April 14, 1912, the Titanic struck an iceberg and eventually sank, killing over 1,500 people.

item.title: Serbia government wants to limit reality TV, adopt 4-day work week
item.description:
Serbia's newly elected, student-led but still leaderless government wants to restrict the amount of reality television aired in the country to just 45 minutes per day, and to make it only available after 11 p.m. on terrestrial TV channels.
The Student List party ousted Serbia's longtime strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic, an ally of Russia's Vladimir Putin, in an October election, promising to end corruption in the Balkan nation.
Subscription channels would still be allowed to carry reality shows, according to the party's plans, published on its website. The party also wants to ban all live reality show broadcasts on the terrestrial channels, and repeats or additional coverage of the shows would count toward the 45-minute maximum.
Broadcasters would be compelled to interrupt reality shows if there is any violence, hate speech, or threats.
Paid channels would not be subject to the restrictions under the plans.
Protesters gather outside a pro-government television station with a national flag during a student-led protest in Belgrade on March 29, 2025, accusing it of spreading propaganda as part of nearly five months of mass demonstrations against the government.
ANDREJ ISAKOVIC
The Student List says it sees reality TV as emblematic of a violent culture espoused under Vucic's authoritarian government. Serbian news channels were long seen as favoring the regime in their coverage.
The Student List, which is deliberately free of hierarchy and has no leader, is still very much getting to grips with the job of governing the country after its election victory.
The new administration is targeting better working conditions and curbs on what it sees as the corrosive influence of reality programming. It also announced plans to institute a 4-day wor...

item.title: High-quality medieval armor discovered in shipwreck that sank in 1495
item.description:
Maritime archaeologists have found pieces of high-quality medieval armor found among the wreckage of a 500-year-old Danish warship, an international team of researchers revealed on Tuesday.
The ship, known as "Griffin" or "Gribshunden," was the warship of Denmark's 15th-century leader King Hans. The ship was also used for diplomatic expeditions. In 1495, there was an explosion that led to the ship catching fire and sinking while anchored north of Sweden's Stora Ekö Island. The wreck was discovered in the 1970s.
In the decades since, the ship has been the subject of frequent study. The latest discovery of the chain mail armor was made by team of experts from the United Kingdom's University of Southampton and Swedish institutions Södertörn University and Stockholm University, who have been conducting joint expeditions of the wreck since 2019.
The team's archaeologists and hydrographic survey specialists were using advanced robotic survey technology and 3-D photogrammetric imaging to make detailed archaeological records of the wreckage when they found the armor fragments, according to a news release from the University of Southampton.
Medieval fine chain mail found on the Griffin.
Florian Huber/Griffin 2026
The chain mail armor is made of copper-alloy, the university said. It was found while documenting an ammunition-tool chest just below the ship's forecastle, which was an elevated fighting platform at the front of the vessel.
Military gear may have been stored in the area, said Dr. Rodrigo Pacheco-Ruiz, a visiting fellow at the University of Southampton's Centre for Maritime Archaeology, in the news release. German mercenaries, known as Landsknechts, were aboard the ship when it sank in 1495, Pacheco-Ruiz said.

item.title: Brits are having less sex, but watching a lot of porn, survey finds
item.description:
London — One-third of Brits between the ages of 16 and 24 have never had sex, according to a large-scale, periodic survey that has studied the prevalence of sexting and pornography use for the first time.
The decline in youth sexual activity is part of a wider trend of British people having less sex compared to previous generations, all revealed in the National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal), a survey of nearly 7,000 Britons between 2022 and 2024, which was published Tuesday in The Lancet medical journal.
Adults aged 45 and below are having sex twice a month on average, down from four times a month in 1990-91, and three in 2010-12, according to the survey. The proportion of 16- to 24-year-olds who said they had never had sex rose from 18% to 38% among women and 18% to 28% among men, compared to the previous Natsal study.
The latest survey was the first time participants had been asked about their online activity.
Half of the women respondents between 16 and 24 said they had watched pornography in the past year, while 86% of young men said they had. Half of 16- to 24-year-olds said they had sent or received sexual images on their phone in the past year.
"There has been an emerging shift towards less sexual experience among young people," wrote the authors of the study. "Sexual lifestyles now commonly incorporate online behaviors such as sexting and pornography, especially for young people."
One of the researchers on the project, Prof. Wendy Macdowall at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, told CBS News partner BBC News that while it may be tempting to link the online activity with the decline in sexual activity, there are several other reasons for the drop, "especially among young people."

item.title: Security forces storm scene, end Colombia supermarket siege
item.description:
Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in the Caribbean city of Cartagena early Wednesday, ending a day-long hostage siege, with the president saying all of those held hostage had been rescued and one captor killed.
Several explosions were heard before security forces entered the building, where about 20 people were believed to have been held by armed men.
"In an extraordinary joint operation between the National Police and the Armed Forces, all the hostages were rescued," President Abelardo de la Espriella said in a video posted on social media.
A Colombian Army soldier is seen in the Exito Supermarket after security forces stormed the building to free hostages held by gunmen in Cartagena, Colombia, in the early hours of Nov. 25, 2026.
AFP via Getty Images
Shortly after midnight, a police helicopter hovered low over the shopping center as security forces massed outside the supermarket, AFP reporters saw.
Explosions then echoed around the complex as tactical teams moved in.
Ten of the roughly 30 people initially held had been released during the 17-hour standoff, including several elderly women.
Moments later, soldiers could be seen inside the Exito supermarket as security forces secured the building.
De la Espriella, who appeared at the scene wearing fatigues and a sidearm while brandishing a walkie-talkie, described the operation as a roaring success.
"We gave them the opportunity to surrender and free the hostages. They rejected that opportunity and we acted decisively," he said, lauding the operation as "absolutely flawless."
The president said one hostage-taker had been killed.

item.title: NATO allies anxious as war spreads beyond Ukraine, Russia borders
item.description:
Some NATO countries are voicing increasing anxiety as hostilities in the nearly five-year war sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine spread beyond the two countries' borders.
Polish authorities accused Russia again Tuesday of deliberately violating the nation's airspace as officials said a surveillance drone briefly crossed the Polish border before turning back into Ukraine. Poland, a member of the U.S.-led NATO alliance and a neighbor and close ally of Ukraine, accused Moscow of a deliberate provocation late last week after three Russian missiles landed on Polish soil.
Polish Deputy Defense Minister Paweł Zalewski said in a radio interview on Tuesday that the Russian drone crossed the border for a "very short time" and was "monitored from the very beginning."
"I spoke with the Operational Command of the Armed Forces, and the decision was made not to shoot it down, as they did not want to risk any casualties or damage on the civilian side," Zalewski told Radio Poland. "We assume this was an intentional act."
A "need for stability in our near areas"
Norway's Defense Minister Tore Sandvik said Tuesday, meanwhile, that the Scandinavian country was speaking with Ukrainian officials about the "need for stability in our near areas," following a strike on Saturday that hit a U.S.-sanctioned Russian cargo ship in international waters in the Gulf of Finland.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy acknowledged Ukraine had carried out that strike in a social media post on Monday, saying the country's forces used seven domestically produced naval drones to attack the ship.
A photo provided by the Finnish Border Guard shows efforts to extinguish a fire on board the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland, Nov. 22, 2026. The ship, under U.S. sanctions for transporting illicit weapons, was attacked by Ukraine using sea drones.

item.title: Prince William and Kate's country home broken into, 2 arrested
item.description:
Two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at the royal family's Sandringham Estate, the country residence of William and Catherine, the Prince and Princess of Wales, U.K. police said.
Police responded to reports of "suspicious activity" at Anmer Hall on King Charles III's Sandringham estate in eastern England Monday at about 6 p.m., Norfolk police said. William and Catherine and the rest of their family weren't present at the time, the police said.
The police said Wednesday that Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, were charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site. They were due in court later Wednesday.
]Police dogs, drones and a helicopter were used to search the property and make the arrests, officials said.
Kensington Palace told CBS News it wouldn't comment on security matters.
Anmer Hall, which has 10 bedrooms, was a wedding present to the couple from Queen Elizabeth II. It is used as a country residence on weekends. William and his family spend most of their time at Forest Lodge in Windsor, which they have described as their "forever home."
The reported break-in came as William visited Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the British leader's office, 10 Downing Street.
Catherine recently opened up about finding hope and joy amid uncertainty in a new documentary exploring life since her cancer diagnosis in 2024.
"Heal" follows the 44-year-old royal as she attempts the Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours. The film will premiere on the BBC in the United Kingdom on Nov. 29, before airing internationally on NBCUniversal in the United States on Nov. 30.
